idiom_name: interface with a single unexported marker method
implementation_notes: Go interfaces are satisfied structurally, so a marker cannot be closed the Java way; the idiomatic substitute is an interface whose only method is unexported - only types in the same package can implement it, turning the marker into a closed set the compiler enforces. Consumers convert to the interface or type-switch on it, and the type switch must cover every member for exhaustiveness. Use it for union-style closed sets and framework-known types; because the method is unexported, external packages cannot join the set, which is exactly the sealing.
pitfalls: An unexported marker method permanently closes the interface to other packages - intentional sealing but a hard extension barrier.
A typed nil pointer stored in the interface satisfies the interface; the type switch matches it and a dereference can panic.
any/interface{} accepts everything and therefore marks nothing; the type switch default branch is the real contract there.

variants.name: Open marker via any plus type switch
variants.idiom_name: any (interface{}) plus a type switch over known concrete types
variants.implementation_notes: When the marked set is genuinely open (plugins, heterogeneous payloads, boundary decoding), the marker degenerates to any/interface{} and the consumer type-switches over the concrete types it knows, with the default case as the fallback. The mark carries no compile-time guarantee, so keep it at boundaries rather than in domain APIs, and prefer a small named interface defined where it is consumed once the set is known.
pitfalls: any accepts every value, so mistakes survive compilation and surface at run time.
Values crossing any normally allocate on the heap, which matters in hot paths.
The type switch silently ignores new member types until someone adds a case - the default branch hides the omission.
